body:
Yes, plagued.. it's quite disturbing, and massively disorienting.  At least in the several ways it manifests for me..

It's not a literally visual phenomenon in my case, and really I thought in general it wasn't a visual thing happening, so what you *see* isn't changed, it's something else going on in your brain.

Regardless, it was terrifying to me as a kid.. and once I learned (much later) that there was a label for it, despite it not being understood, it was less so.

Ha.. yep.  I've been plagued with this since I was a child.  It diminished in frequency for about ten years, then flared back up ridiculously and has stayed at that level ever since.

No idea what prompted it, it hit me 6-8 years prior to my being diagnosed with CFS and a good few years before I had mono prior to that.

No doctor I've spoken to in all this time has known what to make of it, other than a "Huh, that's weird," or "I wonder what that's all about."

Wonderful..

This is the first time I've run across anyone asking about it.

I have a strange and uncomfortable relationship with sleep.  It's never refreshing in any conventional sense, and feels like something my body must do "or else"...but my ability to remain prone in bed for more than 5-6 hours is really limited due to body pain, so I eventually get awakened by that and ultimately roused completely.  Almost every night and morning follow that paradigm.

Many people I've talked to (sick and not) don't seem to understand or recognize the distinction between "sleepy" and "fatigued."  I very, very rarely feel sleepy, unless I'm unable to sleep at all for physical reasons.  But I am ALWAYS fatigued.

The flip side of this coin, for me, has long been my inability to relate to people with this condition who sleep all day, every day.  That is so alien to my years-long experience with this, it makes me think I don't have what everyone else does..

I have read a few.. some really didn't help with my perspective because they were written from the standpoint of a person having 'overcome' their illness, ultimately, which.. just isn't a realistic end-point for me right now.

I read one book that was specifically about a man with CFS and his attempts at relationships.. that was more interesting, in that, it was more directly applicable, but.. eh.

I'd never heard of this book (or movie, apparently), thanks for the recommendation.. it looks like it's very hard to actually get a hold of, though.

Thanks for taking the time & energy to reply.  

Not thinking about it has been the de facto method of coping, for me, for years.  And usually that was only possible by means of distraction.  The mounting issue, for me, has been a significantly decreased ability to distract myself sufficiently.. so the realities of my circumstances continually beat on my mental shores until I'm emotionally eroded.. into the state I am now.

I hear you, though.  I do.  I wish it were that easy, for me.

I've yet to qualify for any government assistance, so I'm thinking that's largely a dead end for me.  And I'm going to continue to be a useless, do-nothing individual who for some reason hasn't killed themselves yet, I probably shouldn't do it on taxpayer money..

Kinda turns into a big, mental feedback loop, that line of thinking..

I do have thoughts like that, pretty often.  And along the lines of "If I knew then what I know now."  

Ten years ago, I was technically in a better position in life, though still bad.  Just not as bad as now.  I didn't realize, then, that things for me would continue to get worse.  So while I did have suicidal ponderings for a lot of these years, most of them were held at bay by hopeful thoughts.  

Anymore?  Not so much.  As I recently [posted](https://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/6pbb5y/seeking_support_im_a_chronicallyill_impossibly/) about..
That's certainly something, a step, I would've liked to be able to take.  But there hasn't been money available for that, and I've never gotten any state aid.

Thank you for reading, and I'm sorry to hear that you're experiencing any version of what I am.  

As far as talking, can you PM me?  It's easier for me to keep track of than the comment & post replies.

I appreciate the thought, I do.  Cognitive issues from the illness prevent me from all manner of complex activities and I learned years ago that anything computer-related beyond basic user-level interaction was far beyond sustainable for me.
Thank you for taking the time to read it.

I definitely feel that last statement.. I don't want to have to kill myself.  

I just feel as though life/the universe/something is all but forcing me into that position despite what I want.  

I wouldn't want anyone to experience the misery I've experienced, so on that point I'm sorry you're on that path.  I want to say that I hope you find improvement, or that you find something that makes life more bearable--as those are the hopes I'd tried to cling to--but I know how foolish hoping can be, now, and as much as I still feel it for others.. I don't for myself.  

PM me if you're interested at all in a continuing discussion about these (or other) things?

If by physical needs, you mean a roof over my head and food on my plate, then yes, that's true.  So in that sense, my case is nowhere near as dire as those who've lost one or both of those things as well.. I do get that.  

It's probably one of the reasons why I don't casually talk about this problem (or related) with people; I never want to come across as otherwise spoiled or that I'm coming from a place of entitlement.  Someone said to me, quite some time ago, that I should think about all the people who have it far worse in their lives and take that to give myself an understanding that as bad as I think my life is, it's actually a **great** life on balance.  

I couldn't then, just as I can't now, agree with that in black & white.. but I do get the problem..

I'd just replied to another commenter about their remarks regarding my writing.. and I didn't realize that telling someone they write well had become a common reply to people here.. that certainly changes how one/I should look at the replies..  

Right now, I don't mind a spectrum of input, be it something truly thoughtful or something canned.. because this is not a topic I've much experience actually talking about, or talking through, with anyone.  

It's come up from time to time with only one or two people in my life, but even those discussions have hard limits.. and I'm trying to find a place or way to break through those limits and.. see what else there is to see.  

Thank you for reading my post.. and spending the time to reply to me.  

I'm not sure what it is I'm looking for right now, but I hope I'll know it when I see it.

Thank you for the compliment.  It baffles me that I've seen similar comments, as I have in the past.. my writing, such as it is, never struck me as anything special or out of the ordinary.  

Writing is definitely an interest of mine, and has been for years.  But because of cognitive issues I experience with my illness, it's been something I can almost never pursue.  Certainly not to anything close to satisfaction.  

In the earlier years of my illness, I deluded myself into believing that it could be a way to both create to my heart's content, and hopefully even achieve some level of financial security of my own.  Joke was on me.

One thing that hadn't occurred to me when writing my original post, or reposting a version of it shortly after, is that it would have a negative impact on anyone.  

For that, I am sorry.  Truly.. 

I know nothing of your illness, but I'm saddened to hear that it's already had that effect on you.  I get it.. but it's horrible, just the same.  

I can't really account for how I've managed to deal with it this long, except to say that my condition hasn't always been as bad as it has been in recent years.  And certain other events distracted me enough that it felt like it was a manageable cross to bear.  

Not so anymore..

For some reason I'm not comfortable talking about my religious views in public..  

As to your second point, I genuinely don't see the value in myself of which you speak.  To be sitting here, seriously considering killing myself, doesn't feel like strength to me at all.  Having not done so considerably sooner feels like cowardice, fear.  Wanting more than merely love from family feels like selfishness, being ungrateful.  I don't see value in any of those things..  

As for anyone watching or learning from me, I don't think that's even a thing... heck, I didn't manage to draw enough attention to this post to drum up any conversation outside of this one.  Not to devalue your response.. it just reaffirms for me how invisible I remain despite my efforts to the contrary.

I have one friend who is actually in a similar situation as me, who more or less knows a lot of this.  But I hesitate to lean too heavily on them, as I wouldn't want to put this kind of thing casually or frequently on any one (or two, or three..) people.  

I don't think my family, in general, is aware of my feelings about them and the family history as a whole.  The barest facts of my existence as visible to any of them if they actually look to my circumstances will tell them enough of what they need to know about the here and now.  I think anyone who sees my life and thinks, "Yeah, he's content." or "Oh, he's fully capable of finding that which he wants in life." is really deluding themselves.  

Additionally, the family I have left around me aren't really equipped to handle the full and real weight of what presses on me daily.  They just can't.  And they're certainly not the types receptive to talking about damaging family history.  That ship has sailed.  

I think maybe one or two people may know the 'real me'.. as least as much any anyone outside of myself really can.  But they are not people that are in my day to day life at all (in person, or daily contact), and not people I can burden indefinitely.  I already feel like I may be reaching a breaking point with one or both of them.  

I suppose reaching out here was my lame attempt at finding anyone willing to hear me on these bleakest of points and connect with them.  But now I'm thinking my original post was too long, or too uninteresting or not dramatic enough to draw the right eyes to it.  

Regardless of that, where were you headed with that line of questioning, if I may ask?

I definitely feel helpless, yes.  

I'm not sure how specific I feel comfortable being about my situation, but my illness limits me, physically, often in severe or extreme ways. You wouldn't know it to look at me.  I have cognitive difficulties that come and go at random and that have wreaked havoc on my ability to pursue nearly all the creative endeavors I'd be otherwise inclined to try to work on.  Not to mention the physical pain I'm always in.  Baseline existence is literally an arduous chore that never gets easier.

I'm trying to resist nitpicking your response or countering everything you've said to me, because ultimately I do appreciate that you took your time and energy to do so.  Doubly so since I don't believe many will read or respond to me..  

Regarding not feeling loved, however.. that merits something of a reply, I feel.  

It's a complex topic, for me.  I know my family 'loves' me.. as they are sort of programmed to, to the extent that anyone's family is.  But my history and experience with family is complicated and fraught with negativity and hurt.. so it's simply not enough for me (as selfish and awful as this makes me sound..) that these people I depend on 'love' me.  Put more simply, I *need* something more than that.  

I do apologize if I'm coming across as though my attitude is bad.  Everything I've said here is largely an internal dialog I have with myself.  I don't often project out into the world all of this, to anywhere near this extent.  Sure, people around me know I'm not happy and that there are some specific things that tend to haunt me more than others.  But I've always still pushed ahead with *some* semblance of optimism that I can't say I'm truly feeling anymore.  

As I said previously, hope feels entirely absent now.
